entries.search: Uranium ditelluride hosts two superconducting states together Cornell researchers found that two superconducting states can coexist in uranium ditelluride under pressure. Ultrasound measurements revised the material’s phase diagram and revealed competition between the states as temperature fell. The result advances research into a candidate for topological superconductivity, while quantum-computing applications remain several steps away. science Science Science 2026-11-01 Two states occupy the same region Cooling allows one state to displace the other A candidate for topological superconductivity Uranium ditelluride hosts two superconducting states together Cornell University Cornell experiment finds coexisting superconducting states in quantum-computing candidate FingerLakes1.com
entries.summary: Cornell researchers found that two superconducting states can coexist in uranium ditelluride under pressure. Ultrasound measurements revised the material’s phase diagram and revealed competition between the states as temperature fell. The result advances research into a candidate for topological superconductivity, while quantum-computing applications remain several steps away.
